rules: Every call goes through the capability interface; the component sits behind an adapter (T-t7-02).
Each harness has a dry-run adapter that runs here and a live adapter driven by env vars; the ledger records which mode produced a result.
Each harness executes one adapter swap with the conformance run before and after (T-t9-06).
Product names appear only inside adapter modules and the env-var table.

harnesses.name: containment
harnesses.adapter_today: Exposes: declared resources, declared egress, and a containment report asserted from outside. Hides: the guest kernel, the boot arguments, the jail layout and the per-VM uid.
harnesses.second_adapter: gVisor, Kata Containers, Cloud Hypervisor, or a hosted sandbox service
harnesses.minimal_call: start one contained unit, run one agent turn over ACP, cancel it, read the stop reason and the containment report

harnesses.name: gateway
harnesses.adapter_today: Exposes: a routing class, a payload, a ceiling, and a claim ticket. Hides: which vendor, which member model, which endpoint, and which key paid for it.
harnesses.second_adapter: OpenRouter, direct provider SDKs, or a serving engine's native API
harnesses.minimal_call: one completion by model class under a scoped key and a cap; a vendor name in the request is refused

harnesses.name: observability
harnesses.adapter_today: Exposes: a span, a metric and a log in a published vocabulary. Hides: the backend, its storage, its queue and its UI.
harnesses.second_adapter: Phoenix, Braintrust, or any OTLP collector - the safest swap on the board
harnesses.minimal_call: one trace whose spans carry the run and root dispatch ids as attributes; reassembled by grouping, not parentage

harnesses.name: workflow
harnesses.blueprint_tool_entry: Temporal (data directory present, server not listening)
harnesses.standard: none for durability; RFC 5545 for recurrence (unverified)
harnesses.adapter_today: Exposes: a step, an idempotency key, a checkpoint and a resume point. Hides: the history format, the workers, the task queues and whether a server exists at all.
harnesses.second_adapter: Restate, DBOS, Inngest, or a queue plus a state machine; the cleanest seam - nothing above it changes
harnesses.minimal_call: one durable flow: a step, a parked approval signal, a bounded loop, a crash, a resume at the first incomplete step

harnesses.name: linked
harnesses.minimal_call: one document through all four doors, contained turn, gateway call, traced, orchestrated; identical envelope and manifest per door

harnesses.name: errors
harnesses.blueprint_tool_entry: absent today per PASS.md B3 (F-b3-13: adopt the RFC directly; the live adapter is an in-process problem factory)
harnesses.adapter_today: Exposes: type, title, status, detail, retryable and the extension members a registered suffix declares. Hides: whether a failure came from the raise site itself or from a wire response reshaped at the edge.
harnesses.second_adapter: an edge component that answers on behalf of a service, per cap-errors-implement's adapters
harnesses.minimal_call: produce one typed problem for a refusal from the closed registry, show a caller deciding to retry or not from the type alone without reading the message, reject a problem whose type is not in the registry, and get byte-identical problem bodies from both adapters

harnesses.name: document-validation
harnesses.blueprint_tool_entry: the in-place keyword-subset checks PASS.md B3 names today (F-b3-09; examples/end-to-end/run.py carries one)
harnesses.adapter_today: Exposes: validate, check_schema, prepare and dialect_in_effect over a schema resource and dialect. Hides: which checker walked the schema, and whether it was read fresh or compiled ahead of use.
harnesses.second_adapter: any 2020-12 validator with a different execution model (F-b3-09): compile-once-then-check versus walk-per-document
harnesses.minimal_call: validate one envelope against examples/end-to-end/schemas/entry.schema.json, get one typed outcome with the failing pointer for a malformed envelope, refuse a schema that declares a dialect other than 2020-12, and show both adapters give the same outcome on the same fixtures
harnesses.status: dry-run measured, live measured (DOCVALID_SCHEMA_STORE_DIR set on this host)

harnesses.name: idempotency
harnesses.blueprint_tool_entry: key on the wire, no lease (PASS.md B3, F-b3-16)
harnesses.standard: Idempotency-Key header convention (draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header-07 on file, unverified)
harnesses.adapter_today: Exposes: a fold over an append-only log at entry, so a completed key answers duplicate with its stored result. Hides: nothing takes the key before execution starts, so it cannot answer a duplicate while the first copy is still running, and cannot stop two concurrent copies from both executing.
harnesses.minimal_call: submit one unit of work with a key, replay it and get the stored result with no second side effect, race two submissions with the same key and show one wins the lease and the other waits or is refused with a typed problem, and show a key reused with a different payload is refused
harnesses.status: dry-run measured, live measured against an on-disk ledger

harnesses.name: capability-packaging
harnesses.blueprint_tool_entry: the skill files PASS.md B3 names today (F-b3-07; this repository's .claude/skills/ directories are the live instance)
harnesses.standard: Agent Skills packaging spec (unversioned on file)
harnesses.adapter_today: Exposes: an identity, a trigger for the body tier, and one reference path for the reference tier. Hides: the filesystem path or registry host a package resolved from, and which loader answered.
harnesses.second_adapter: any spec-conformant registry (F-b3-07): a content-addressed loader that fetches by name and version constraint
harnesses.minimal_call: discover one package by name, read its two required resident fields, load it at each of the three tiers, refuse a package missing a required field with a typed problem, and show the same package resolved by digest from the second loader
harnesses.status: dry-run measured, live measured, second-adapter network form claimed

harnesses.name: policy
harnesses.blueprint_tool_entry: OPA (Rego) — named as the adapter today (F-b3-11); conformance checks exist, not wired into the enforcement path (F-a6-04)
harnesses.standard: Rego / OPA decision API (OPA 1.0 on file, search-sourced)
harnesses.adapter_today: Exposes: a JSON decision request and a JSON decision. Hides: the policy language, the bundle and the engine.
harnesses.second_adapter: Cedar or any policy engine with a decision API (F-b3-11)
harnesses.minimal_call: ask one decision for a unit of work with its actor, tenant and intended action, get allow or a typed deny with the rule that fired, prove the gate cannot be declined by a caller, and show the same decision from the second engine

harnesses.name: work-intake
harnesses.blueprint_tool_entry: the four producers PASS.md B3 names today: CLI, git event, HTTP, schedule (F-b3-08)
harnesses.standard: A2A messaging and CloudEvents (versions on file unverified)
harnesses.adapter_today: Exposes: one canonical envelope, one acknowledgement carrying the entry id, the correlation id and the job digest, and a typed refusal. Hides: the transport, the producer's format, the request identifier, the repository ref, the command line and the message identifier.
harnesses.second_adapter: any conformant producer (F-b3-08): a CloudEvents or A2A producer normalised by a different path
harnesses.minimal_call: drive one document through the human, event, schedule and external doors and show one identical envelope, one identical resolved manifest, and a typed refusal for a malformed task; a replay with the same idempotency key is free

harnesses.name: provenance
harnesses.blueprint_tool_entry: append-only JSONL evidence store (the JSONL evidence records PASS.md B3 names; kb/ledger.jsonl is the live instance of that shape)
harnesses.standard: in-toto Statement v1 in a DSSE envelope with SLSA predicates (versions on file unverified)
harnesses.adapter_today: Exposes: a signed envelope over an in-toto Statement binding a subject digest to the code version, inputs and actor, a location a third party fetches it from, and a verdict from the envelope alone. Hides: the key, the store, the record layout and the file.
harnesses.minimal_call: produce one signed statement binding an artifact digest to the code version, inputs and actor that produced it, verify it with a verifier that reads only the statement, show that editing one byte of the artifact fails verification, and store and fetch it from the second store
harnesses.status: dry-run measured, live measured against the evidence records on this host

harnesses.name: tool-access
harnesses.blueprint_tool_entry: the MCP endpoint PASS.md A6 records as live and authenticated with zero tools registered (F-a6-03)
harnesses.standard: Model Context Protocol (version on file: 2026-07-28, unverified)
harnesses.adapter_today: Exposes: a catalogue discovered at bind, a tool descriptor with an input schema and a declared effect, one call, one cancel and a health answer that counts. Hides: which server implements a tool, where it runs, over what transport, and whose credential paid for it.
harnesses.minimal_call: discover the callable tools, check one call's arguments against the tool's declared input schema, make the call, cancel a second call mid-flight, and read a health check that counts registered tools rather than answering green

harnesses.name: state-persistence
harnesses.blueprint_tool_entry: the JSONL plus hash chain PASS.md B3 names today (F-b3-17; kb/ledger.jsonl and tools/kb.py are the live instance)
harnesses.standard: no standard to adopt (F-b3-17, F-b5-04, F-b5-05); the record proof shape follows RFC 9162 with RFC 8785 canonicalization where the skill says so
harnesses.adapter_today: Exposes: an opaque record, an expected head, a fencing token, and the record's id and new head on success. Hides: the file, its byte layout, and whether a compare-and-swap exists underneath.
harnesses.second_adapter: an object store, a relational store or an event log (F-b3-17): pick one with a different execution model and stub its transport
harnesses.minimal_call: put one opaque record, read it back at a pinned snapshot while a later write lands, get an inclusion proof for that one record that verifies without the whole log, and show two concurrent appenders never produce a fork

harnesses.name: identity
harnesses.blueprint_tool_entry_note: absent today per PASS.md B3 (F-b3-14): no identity component runs on this host and PASS.md A6 records no identity field anywhere in the system (F-a6-05). adapters/live.py is therefore a stub that says so, reached through the environment variables that would name an issuer or a workload API socket.
harnesses.standard: OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693) and workload identity, SPIFFE/SPIRE shape (versions on file unverified)
harnesses.adapter_today: Exposes: an actor, a delegation chain, a scope, one audience and an expiry. Hides: the issuer, the trust material, the credential bytes and whether verification cost a network call.
harnesses.minimal_call: obtain a workload identity for one unit of work, exchange it for a delegated token scoped to one downstream call with a shorter lifetime, show the delegation chain of three hops on the token, and get a typed refusal when a hop tries to widen scope

harnesses.name: memory
harnesses.blueprint_tool_entry: absent today: PASS.md's inventory of what is defined but not running is stated because an inventory that omits this is not an inventory (F-a6-01), and memory is in none of its rows; the live adapter is a stub reached through env vars naming a store path
harnesses.standard: none found (A-standard-agent-memory-no-ratified-standard-found); the binding record and recall shapes are this repo's design
harnesses.adapter_today: Exposes: remember, recall, supersede, forget over a scope, a body, a kind, provenance and a staleness policy. Hides: which store answered, its endpoint, its index, its ranker, its file layout.
harnesses.second_adapter: a store that answers by exact scope key, per cap-memory-implement's adapters
harnesses.minimal_call: write one item under a binding record with a scope and an expiry, recall it by scope, show an expired item is not recalled, show an item written under another scope is not recalled, and show the same recall from both stores

harnesses.name: capability-registry
harnesses.blueprint_tool_entry: today's resolution by directory path in this repository (.claude/skills/ and docs/skill-manifest.json; F-b3-07)
harnesses.standard: MCP Registry API v0.1, in preview (unverified; A-standard-mcp-registry-api)
harnesses.adapter_today: Exposes: resolve, list_versions, describe, publish, verify over a signed, hash-chained index. Hides: the directory layout, the index file format, and which store answered.
harnesses.second_adapter: a content-addressed store fetching records over a network, per cap-capability-registry-implement's adapters; a faithful stub
harnesses.minimal_call: publish one signed record for a package, resolve it by name and a version constraint, verify the digest matches the package, show a record cannot be edited in place (a second publish is a new version), roll back to the previous version, and refuse a record whose signature does not verify
harnesses.status: dry-run measured, live measured, second-adapter claimed (faithful stub, no live network route)

harnesses.name: human-interaction
harnesses.blueprint_tool_entry: approve.service - the approval unit that already runs as PASS.md A2 records it (F-a2-01)
harnesses.standard: AG-UI agent-to-user interaction events (no protocol version string found on file, search-only; A-standard-ag-ui-agent-to-user-interaction-events)
harnesses.adapter_today: Exposes: an ask with a deadline and a response schema, four decisions, and a resume on the run's own correlation id. Hides: the phone, the network it is on, and who is holding it.
harnesses.second_adapter: a streaming browser client behind the same interface, per cap-human-interaction-implement's adapters; a faithful stub is acceptable
harnesses.minimal_call: park one run on an ask with a deadline, deliver a decision through the first surface, resume the run, show a second decision for the same ask is refused as a replay, show a decision after the deadline is refused with a typed problem, and show identity and correlation stamped on the pause and the resume

harnesses.name: evaluation
harnesses.blueprint_tool_entry: observe-langfuse-web-1 (F-a1-05) - the trace backend every run already lands in; PASS.md has no Evaluation row, so the store is what the capability binds to today
harnesses.standard: none adopted; the case-set, replay and verdict shapes are this repo's design (cite the X- research records cap-evaluation names)
harnesses.adapter_today: Exposes: a case set reference, a rubric handle, a trajectory, a three-valued outcome and a per-case transition. Hides: the metric implementations, the score thresholds, where the corpus and the records are stored, and whether a collector is running at all.
harnesses.second_adapter: a fixture replayer with no collector and no server, per cap-evaluation-implement's adapters
harnesses.minimal_call: register one case set, replay one recorded run against it, score the trajectory, get a verdict with the case that failed named, and prove a gate cannot report success with every case skipped (executed_cases must be counted)

harnesses.name: scheduling
harnesses.blueprint_tool_entry: the engine-owned schedules PASS.md B3 names today (F-b3-15, Temporal schedules)
harnesses.standard: RFC 5545 recurrence rules (on file unverified; A-standard-rfc-5545-recurrence-rules)
harnesses.adapter_today: Exposes: occurrences, next_after (the shared pure evaluator), declare and fire over a recurrence string, an anchor and an IANA zone. Hides: the engine's own timer, its calendar-spec encoding, and whether a server is listening at all.
harnesses.second_adapter: a standalone recurrence evaluator that computes occurrences as a pure call, per cap-scheduling-implement's adapters; cron or any RFC 5545 parser (F-b3-15)
harnesses.minimal_call: evaluate one recurrence rule with a time zone and a window as a pure call, get the occurrence set, fire one occurrence as an entry through the same envelope every other door uses (reuse examples/end-to-end/schemas/entry.schema.json and entries/schedule.json), show a DST-forward gap, a DST-back repeat, a leap day and a BYSETPOS rule against a vector corpus of more than 40 vectors, and show both adapters produce identical occurrence sets
